clue.text: Intelligent woman moved guest in block

indicators.note: the letters of guest, in and block are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A guest is shifted into another block of rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moved' is the anagram signal: GUEST IN BLOCK rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bluestocking is a scholarly or literary woman, a term from an 18th-century London society of learned ladies.

clue.text: Glancing sideways, summon general first

indicators.note: the general is told to come first, ahead of the word for summon

parts.note: Robert E. Lee, the Confederate general, is crossword shorthand for a general
to ring someone is to call or summon them

explanation.surface: Someone shoots a sidelong look before calling for the general.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue names summon before general, but 'first' moves the general to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Leering means looking slyly or lasciviously out of the corner of the eye.

clue.text: Request feast in eastern US city

indicators.note: the feast word is placed inside the letters for eastern and the US city

parts.note: NY is New York
a treat is a special meal or feast

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a banquet to be held in an East Coast American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a container signal here: the feast goes inside the eastern-plus-city pair.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or request.

clue.text: Mood in school after head moves south

indicators.note: in a down entry the first letter of the school drops to the bottom

parts.note: Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: The atmosphere at a school changes once its headteacher relocates south.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON's first letter goes to the end, giving TONE; 'head' is the first letter, not a headteacher.
explanation.definitionFit: Tone is the general feeling or atmosphere of a place, its mood.

clue.text: Fully employ Celt for labouring

indicators.note: the letters of employ and Celt are worked over and rearranged

explanation.surface: Hire a Celtic worker to do manual labour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'labouring' is the anagram signal for EMPLOY + CELT; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Completely and fully both mean entirely, to the whole extent.

clue.text: Very cold home, one with unending darkness

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the word for darkness loses its final letter, so it has no end

parts.note: gloom means darkness

explanation.surface: A single person lives in endless darkness, like a polar winter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unending' trims the final letter from the darkness word; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An igloo is an Inuit dwelling built of snow blocks, home in a freezing climate.

clue.text: Old relative joined by a lawyer in Spanish city

parts.note: a gran is a grandmother, an elderly relative
DA is a District Attorney, an American prosecuting lawyer

explanation.surface: A grandmother travels with a lawyer to a city in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: GRAN + A + DA in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Granada is a city in Andalusia, home of the Alhambra.

clue.text: Lure cop to hire trained investigator

indicators.note: the letters of the first four words are trained into a new shape

explanation.surface: A detective is tempted by an offer to employ a police officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trained' is the anagram signal for LURE COP TO HIRE; the paper's copy read 'top', which lacks the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Hercule Poirot is Agatha Christie's famous Belgian private detective.

clue.text: Main horse that collapsed gets positive injection

indicators.note: the letters of the three words fall down and are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: The chief racehorse that fell is given a jab by the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' is the anagram signal for MAIN HORSE THAT; 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A boost or stimulus is called this idiom, literally a jab given in the upper limb.

clue.text: Girl and boy retaining time for football team

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name

indicators.note: the girl and boy names hold the time letter between them

parts.note: Ron is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A young couple keep their time free to support a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retaining' means the two names hold the time letter between them; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Everton is a Premier League football club based in Liverpool.

clue.text: Artist and philosopher with excellent son

parts.note: John Stuart Mill was a British philosopher
A1 means first-rate, written as AI in crosswords

explanation.surface: A painter and a thinker appear alongside a fine young man.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-rate) is written AI, the figure 1 standing in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John Everett Millais was a Victorian painter, a founder of the Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood.

clue.text: One sitting in Merc recharged battery perhaps

indicators.note: the letter for one sits inside the rearranged car name
the letters of the car brand are charged up again in a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone sits in a Mercedes whose battery has just been recharged.
explanation.walkthrough: MERC rearranged gives CRME, with I sitting inside it; 'battery' is the offence of assault and battery, not a car battery.
explanation.definitionFit: Battery, unlawful physical attack on a person, is an example of an offence.

clue.text: Director in part retired faces difficulty -finding area of great wealth?

indicators.note: the first group of letters stands in front of, facing, the word for difficulty
the director letter goes inside the turned-round word for part
the word for part retires, going back the way it came

parts.note: a role is a part in a play
ado means fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A film director, partly retired, runs into trouble in his search for riches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses the part word (giving ELOR), 'in' puts the director inside it, and 'faces' sets it before the difficulty; the hyphen before 'finding' is a print artefact.
explanation.definitionFit: El Dorado was the legendary city of gold sought by Spanish conquistadors, so any place of fabulous riches.

clue.text: Introduction from Irishman with fidgety niece showing restlessness

parts.note: a typical Irishman, Pat, introducing himself would say I'm Pat

indicators.note: the letters of niece fidget into a new order

explanation.surface: An Irishman's introduction comes with a restless niece in tow.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'introduction' is a self-introduction, "I'm Pat" (Pat being the stock crossword Irishman), followed by NIECE rearranged as IENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Impatience is an inability to wait calmly, a state of restlessness.

clue.text: Genuine friend leaving north after part of course

indicators.note: the trimmed friend word comes after the part of course

parts.note: a leg is one stage of a course or journey

indicators.note: the north letter leaves the word for friend

parts.note: an intimate is a close friend

explanation.surface: A real friend heads off away from the north partway through a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of course' is a stage of a race or journey, and 'leaving' drops the north letter from the friend word.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means authentic, lawful or real, as genuine does.

clue.text: Some fix a tariff retrospectively for transport

indicators.note: looking back, the run of letters is read from right to left
only some of the letters of fix a tariff are taken, a run inside them

explanation.surface: An authority sets a charge for transport backdated to an earlier time.
explanation.walkthrough: IXAT, from fIX A Tariff, read backwards gives the answer; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxi is a hired car, a means of getting about.

clue.text: Concern in cricket match about English skipper's 'finale

indicators.note: the cricket match word goes about, around, the English letter and the skipper's last letter

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: finale means the last letter of the word skipper's is taken

explanation.surface: Worry in a Test match about how the England captain will finish.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is a full international cricket match, chiefly a British and Commonwealth fixture; 'about' wraps it round English plus the skipper's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An interest is a concern or stake in something, as in a matter of concern to you.

clue.text: Praise flaky cake

definitions.meaning: extravagant commendation, as of a book on its jacket
a light hollow pastry, e.g. a jam or cream one

explanation.surface: Paying a compliment to some light pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff is an exaggerated, flattering review, and also a light cake of pastry, as in cream puff.

clue.text: Much of titled figure is featured in paper -a source of bouquets?

indicators.note: the trimmed figure and is are featured inside the paper's letters

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, the paper where this crossword runs

indicators.note: only much of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a lord is a person with a title

explanation.surface: A peer is the subject of a newspaper story about bouquets of praise.
explanation.walkthrough: FT is the Financial Times, this puzzle's own paper; 'Much of' trims the titled figure's last letter and 'featured in' puts the result inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sells or arranges flowers is where bunches of blooms come from.

clue.text: Dispute? Fault distributed about poor language!

indicators.note: the rearranged fault letters go around the poor language
the letters of fault are distributed into a new order

parts.note: lingo is a slang, often slighting word for a language or jargon

explanation.surface: A row breaks out when blame is spread around for some bad language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' rearranges fault as FA...UT, split so that 'about' can wrap it round the poor language.
explanation.definitionFit: A falling-out is a quarrel or disagreement between people.

clue.text: Outside broadcast spectacle that's offensive

parts.note: OB is the broadcasting abbreviation for an outside broadcast
a scene is a sight or spectacle

explanation.surface: A live TV programme from the field shows a shocking spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: OB + SCENE; 'that's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscene means indecent or repugnant, offending accepted standards.

clue.text: Like a sports drink? No cost possibly to consume one after start of innings

indicators.note: the rest comes after the first letter of innings
the first letter of innings is taken
the rearranged letters eat, consume, the letter for one
possibly signals that no and cost might be rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A drink for sportsmen might be free, consumed after the first innings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges no cost as SOTONC, which 'to consume' wraps round the letter for one; 'after' puts that behind the first letter of innings.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotonic sports drinks have the same salt concentration as body fluids.

clue.text: Postponed outing's beginning above French city

indicators.note: in a down entry the first letter sits above the city
beginning means the first letter of outing's is taken

parts.note: Nice is a city on the French Riviera

explanation.surface: A trip is delayed before setting off for the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: O + NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans put on ice are shelved or suspended for later.

clue.text: Result when bathroom loses appeal

indicators.note: the bathroom word loses the letters for appeal

parts.note: an en suite is a bathroom attached to a bedroom
it is slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: What happens when a bathroom stops being attractive.
explanation.walkthrough: ENSUITE minus IT; 'it' in the sense of sex appeal is an old-fashioned usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, to result.

clue.text: Queen in Geneva offering broad smile

indicators.note: the queen letter is placed in the Geneva word

parts.note: Geneva, or genever, is an old name for gin
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: Her Majesty, visiting Switzerland, beams widely.
explanation.walkthrough: Geneva is not the city: it is the old name (from Dutch genever) for gin.
explanation.definitionFit: A grin is a wide smile.

clue.text: View round wing

parts.note: O is round in shape
a pinion is a bird's wing

explanation.surface: A view on a circular wing of a building.
explanation.walkthrough: O + PINION.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a view or belief held about something.

clue.text: Sound of line followed by cherished animals

indicators.note: signals that the words for line and cherished are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: row means a line, and dear means cherished

explanation.surface: The noise of a queue followed by beloved creatures.
explanation.walkthrough: ROW and DEAR spoken sound like ROE DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe deer are a small Eurasian species of deer, so they are wild beasts.

clue.text: Article followed by European probing foreign currency? Figure goes round hotel immediately

indicators.note: the article comes first and the rest follows it

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the European letter probes into the currency word

parts.note: the rand is South Africa's currency

indicators.note: the figure word goes round the hotel letter

parts.note: ten is a number, a figure
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about foreign exchange sees a figure circling a hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: THE + R(E)AND + T(H)EN.
explanation.definitionFit: There and then means on the spot, at once, without delay.
